name: ANSI/IEEE surge arrester symbol
summary: IEEE-oriented surge arrester symbol connected between a line and ground to limit transient overvoltage.
description: Single-line diagrams in US practice show the surge arrester between a phase conductor and ground, commonly at transformer terminals, cable risers and line entrances. The publisher's IEEE miscellaneous preview lists a surge diverter or lightning arrester form, the counterpart of the existing IEC page.

This illustration explains the connection and is not the IEEE graphic. Arrester class, rated and continuous operating voltages and energy capability come from the equipment data. Lead length between the arrester and protected equipment matters greatly and is not visible on a single-line diagram.
readingNotes: Check arrester location relative to the protected equipment.
Read voltage rating against system earthing.
drawingChecklist: State arrester class and voltage rating.
Keep arrester leads short in layout.
distinction: A surge arrester limits overvoltage; a spark gap is a simpler breakdown element with no valve resistor.
